For the lowest-cost hardware wallet that supports both Ethereum and Solana, compare entry-level models—but verify support for both networks on the exact model before buying. I can’t reliably name today’s cheapest option without current prices and compatibility information.

Compare total delivered cost, including shipping, taxes and any required accessories. Check whether Ethereum and Solana work through the manufacturer’s app or require a compatible third-party wallet, and whether that setup works with your phone or computer. Token support and staking features may differ from basic network support.

A hardware wallet keeps signing keys separate from your everyday device, reducing exposure to malware, but adds cost and setup friction. It does not protect you from approving a malicious transaction or sharing your recovery phrase. A mobile/software wallet is generally free and more convenient, but keeps keys on an internet-connected device. For small balances, it may be a practical starting point; for larger or long-term holdings, hardware isolation can justify the expense.

Buy directly from the manufacturer or an authorized seller. Initialize it yourself, never use a supplied recovery phrase, and keep your recovery backup offline. The best budget choice is the lowest total-cost model with verified support for both chains and a setup you can use safely.
